raw_response:
I am 63, and I have farmed all my life, so I do not like taking big risks. With 20 mu, some family labor away from home, and well irrigation available, I will keep the plan simple and steady. I will put 8 mu into cotton as my main cash crop, and I will use the other 12 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, because that gives me grain from two seasons and spreads my risk. I will not chase the highest possible yield with heavy inputs. I will use seeds I trust, fertilizer at moderate levels, and irrigation only when the crop really needs it, because I have to control costs and labor. For wheat, I will use improved seed, enough base fertilizer, and about three irrigations, since wheat here responds well to water at key stages. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed and a simpler no-tillage or very light establishment to save labor and catch the season quickly. For cotton, I will stay with improved seed, moderate fertilizer, several irrigations from the well, and more pesticide sprays than grain crops because cotton usually needs closer pest control. Overall, I will farm in a cautious way: stable yields, manageable labor, and no extreme spending.
